chunks: Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Shammun, from Abdullah ibn Abd al-Rahman al-Asamm, from Mismāʿ ibn Abd al-Malik, from Abi Abdillah عليه السلام: “Amir al-Mu'minin عليه السلام was brought a man upon whom a hadd had become due, while he had wounds, illness, and the like, so he said:
Amir al-Mu'minin عليه السلام said: “Delay him until he recovers. Do not reopen his wounds upon him lest he die. But when he recovers, we shall administer the hadd to him.”

Muhammad ibn al-Hasan said: There is no contradiction between these two reports and the reports we mentioned earlier that the Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم struck a sick person with a date-palm branch containing one hundred stalks. That is because when establishing the hadd belongs to the Imam, he carries it out according to what he deems appropriate. So if the public interest requires carrying it out immediately, he administers it in a manner that does not lead to the destruction of his life, as the Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم did. And if the public interest requires delaying it, he delays it until he recovers, then carries out the hadd upon him in full.

key_terms.الْإِمَامِ: the legitimate authority responsible for carrying out the hadd
key_terms.الْكَمَالِ: full and complete execution of the punishment once recovery occurs
key_terms.الْمَصْلَحَةُ: the relevant consideration of welfare or proper interest in enforcement
key_terms.تَأْخِيرَهَا: delaying the punishment until a later time
key_terms.قُرُوحُهُ: his wounds, which may be aggravated by punishment
key_terms.يَبْرَأَ: to recover or heal from illness or injury

ai.seo_question: Can a hadd punishment be delayed if the offender is sick or wounded?
ai.summary: This report states that the hadd punishment should be delayed for a wounded or ill person if immediate enforcement would worsen his wounds or lead to death. It also explains that the Imam may determine whether to delay the hadd or carry it out in a modified manner, according to what is required by maslahat.
